newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Rally draws 15,000 to oppose Bangladesh leader.
newsitem.headline: Rally draws 15,000 to oppose Bangladesh leader.

text.p: About 15,000 supporters of the main opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) staged a rally in Dhaka on Tuesday to protest against the policies of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina.
"We demand that terrorism and partisan rule pursued by the government must stop immediately," BNP's secretary-general Abdul Mannan Bhuiyan told the rally.
"Otherwise we will be forced to call a national movement to bring down Sheikh Hasina's government," he said.
Amid cheers and slogans, Bhuiyan said at least 100 BNP workers had been killed by what he said were pro-government "terrorists" since Hasina came to power in June.
It was BNP's first major event since it lost to Hasina's Awami League in the June 12 general election.

Bhuiyan said the election was rigged to ensure the league's victory and that no election as long Hasina remains in office would be impartial. He demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Abu Hena.

Tuesday's BNP rally was also addressed by former energy minister Mosharraf Hossain and several others who said BNP might go for a "bigger movement" next month unless Hasina's government "ended repressive policies and behaved democratically."
